answers.1_schedule_driven: AGREE. Type identity from the plan mark, nominal size from the schedule, geometry as validation. The A2 rectangle-first rule lost F / FN / F10 for detector reasons, not source reasons. One condition: a mark must be read reliably (a text on the structural text layer whose value parses to exactly one schedule type) and the schedule row must be admitted (the table read COMPLETE).
answers.2_type_identity: The plan mark: a text inside the plan's sheet region whose value parses to a schedule type (composite 'C3/F3' gives a column identity AND a footing identity). Never position, never size, never nearest outline.
answers.3_nominal_dimensions: The admitted schedule row for that type (cm header note -> m), per element class: footing L / W / H; column B x D per storey band (FOUNDATION / GF / 1F / 2F&TOP); beam B x D. An explicit local dimension positively bound to the occurrence is the only other source.
answers.4_plan_geometry: Validation only: occurrence location, outline consistency (CONFIRMED / INTERRUPTED / CONFLICT), orientation, measurable length where the element needs one (strap / beam span between supports), relationship to adjacent elements (straps, neighbouring footings, columns carried). Geometry also supplies what the schedule cannot: beam and strap lengths, slab areas.
answers.5_override: Only an explicit local dimension or detail positively bound to that exact occurrence (a DIMENSION whose definition points lie on that outline, or a size text on that element). A drawn outline is evidence: when ONE source outline unambiguously belongs to one tag and agrees, it confirms; when it encloses two typed tags and matches neither schedule, it is a CONFLICT that blocks (never an override, never ignored).
answers.6_strap_interrupted: YES - CASE B. When the tag is securely typed, the tag lies in (or is count-uniquely bound to) an outline whose drawn extent agrees with the schedule and whose interruption is explained by an adjacent element (strap / tie entry gap, notch where a neighbouring footing sits), the schedule quantity is computed with state SCHEDULE_AUTHORITY_INTERRUPTED_GEOMETRY. Adjacent overlap areas are recorded, not deducted silently.
answers.7_distinguish: SCHEDULE_AUTHORITY: admitted schedule row for the parsed tag type. EXPLICIT_LOCAL_OVERRIDE: a dimension / size text bound by its own geometry to that occurrence. APPARENT_GEOMETRY_CONFLICT: one source outline bound to the tag whose extent contradicts the schedule (combined outline holding several typed tags, or a single-tag outline of another size) -> REVIEW / BLOCKED with both values shown. DETECTOR_FALSE_POSITIVE: a candidate assembled by the matcher from several source entities (clipping at a strap, footing + strap union) - rejected and recorded, never quantity authority.
answers.8_cause_1.50x1.40: The A2 template matcher clipped the single H6939 combined outline (3.25 x 1.40) at the 0.70 m strap entry: the east part is 1.50 x 1.40 (see forensics).

16_disagreements: 'Do not lose the quantity merely because the rectangle detector cannot close' - agreed, but F10 is not a detector-only failure: the source draws one combined outline over two typed tags, so forcing both schedule rectangles into the total would double-count their overlap and contradict the drawing; it is blocked with one owner question.

Count-first is right, but a count alone is not a quantity: every counted occurrence still needs its own row with a geometry state; a tag sitting in a conflicting outline is counted and blocked, not silently computed.

The column schedule's FOUNDATION size is not automatically the column size for every storey; per-storey sections come from the storey bands of the schedule, and the column plan's printed sizes disagree with the schedule for about 5 occurrences - reported, not overridden.
The Salon 3.65 m height is an estimate; it is not 'source evidence' for any other height, and its 0.60 m beam-depth assumption is not adopted as a beam depth.
Kitchen / pantry joinery must be an engine inference; the prompt is right to forbid an owner fact here.
